Panel (a): teal curve y = f(x), a gentle concave-down arc that starts just right of the y-axis high up and falls slowly, ENDING shortly after x_k (it does not run to the right edge of the panel)

Panel (a): shaded teal rectangle R_k standing on the x-axis, left edge at x_{k-1}, right edge at x_k, top edge horizontal and grazing the curve (top-left corner just above the curve, top-right corner just below it)
Panel (a): thin gray outline on the rectangle with large italic label 'R_k' centered inside it
Panel (a): tick marks and labels 'x_{k-1}' and 'x_k' below the x-axis at the rectangle's two edges
Panel (a): small circular rotation arrow (flattened ellipse) encircling the y-axis near its top, arrowhead indicating revolution about the y-axis
Panel (a): boxed caption 'Rectangle approximating the k th strip' below the drawing, with italic panel label '(a)' beneath it
Panel (b) [right half of frame]: 3D axonometric view — x-axis receding to the right with arrowhead and label 'x', vertical y-axis through the center of the shell with arrowhead and label 'y'

Panel (b): hollow cylindrical shell S_k — outer cylindrical wall of radius x_k, inner wall (hole) of radius x_{k-1}, top annulus and bottom annulus, drawn as translucent pale gray with dark parallel-ellipse silhouette edges at top and bottom of both walls
Panel (b): the generating rectangle shown teal-tinted on the near-right of the shell, lying in the xy-plane, marking the swept cross-section
Panel (b): teal curve y = f(x) arcing over the top-right of the shell so the shell top is seen meeting the curve
Panel (b): large italic label 'S_k' placed just to the right of the shell at mid-height, with a short leader line
Panel (b): boxed caption 'Cylindrical shell generated by the rectangle' below the drawing, with italic panel label '(b)' beneath it
Optional (off by default): faint nested partition rings for the other n−1 strips, plus a ghost lathe surface of the full solid of revolution
Readout panel: r = x̄_k, h = f(x̄_k), Δx, and V_k = 2πr·h·Δx, with the running sum ΣV_k versus the exact volume

interactions.teaches: that the flat rectangle of panel (a) and the hollow tube of panel (b) are the same object before and after revolution about the y-axis
interactions.label: View

interactions.teaches: that the shell is literally the rectangle dragged around the y-axis — at 0° it is still the flat rectangle R_k, at 360° it has closed into the tube S_k
interactions.label: Revolution angle (deg)

interactions.teaches: that strips of equal thickness sitting at different distances from the axis sweep very different volumes — an outer strip makes a big shell, an inner one a small shell
interactions.label: Strip index k

interactions.label: Highlight factor

interactions.label: Show all n shells

interactions.teaches: that thinner strips give thinner shells and a sum that converges to the exact volume
interactions.label: Number of strips n

demo_steps.title: The two panels side by side
demo_steps.narration: On the left, the region under y = f(x) is cut into vertical strips and the k th strip is approximated by the rectangle R_k. On the right, that same rectangle spun about the y-axis has become the cylindrical shell S_k.

demo_steps.title: The k th rectangle
demo_steps.narration: Look at panel (a) alone: R_k runs from x_{k-1} to x_k and its top edge just grazes the curve. The small rotation arrow at the top of the y-axis reminds you the region will be spun about that axis.

demo_steps.title: Revolve it
demo_steps.narration: Drag the revolution angle from 0° to 360°. The rectangle sweeps a fan, then closes into a tube with inner radius x_{k-1}, outer radius x_k and height f(x̄_k). Orbit to see the hollow core.

demo_steps.title: Where 2πr·h·Δx comes from
demo_steps.narration: Highlight each factor in turn. Unrolling the wall gives a flat slab of width 2πr, height h and thickness Δx — so the shell's volume is the product of those three.

demo_steps.title: Same thickness, different radius
demo_steps.narration: Slide k inward and outward. The thickness Δx never changes but the radius does, so outer shells contribute far more volume than inner ones — the factor x in 2πx f(x) is doing real work.

demo_steps.title: Nesting the shells
demo_steps.narration: Turn on all n shells and raise n. The nested tubes fill the solid and ΣV_k = Σ2πx̄_k f(x̄_k)Δx closes in on the exact volume 2π∫₀^{3.2} x f(x) dx ≈ 67.0.

plan.geometry_notes:
FUNCTION: f(x) = 2.8 − 0.14x² on 0 ≤ x ≤ 3.2 (f(0)=2.8, f(3.2)=1.37) — a GENTLE, nearly flat concave-down arc, NOT a steep decay. Δx = 3.2/n; strip k spans [(k−1)Δx, kΔx]; midpoint x̄_k; rectangle height h = f(x̄_k); V_k = 2π x̄_k f(x̄_k) Δx; exact total 2π∫₀^{3.2} x(2.8−0.14x²)dx = 2π(10.666) ≈ 67.02.
FRAME LAYOUT (default 'Both'): panel (a) occupies the LEFT half, panel (b) the RIGHT half, their baselines aligned; each caption box sits centered under its own drawing with the italic '(a)' / '(b)' beneath. The pair should fill ~0.74 of the frame height — zoom in so text is prominent.
PANEL (a) (flat, front-on, z = 0): y-axis vertical at x = 0 spanning y = −0.3…3.4 with arrowhead up and italic 'y' at its upper right; x-axis horizontal along y = 0 spanning x = −0.5…4.0 with arrowhead right and italic 'x' just above its right end. THE CURVE IS DRAWN ONLY FROM x ≈ 0.45 TO x ≈ x_k + 0.55 (default ≈ 3.2) — it starts in mid-air near the y-axis and stops shortly after the rectangle's right edge; it never reaches the x-axis. Rectangle R_k sits on the x-axis, left edge at x_{k-1}, right edge at x_k, top edge horizontal at height f(x̄_k) so it pokes slightly above the curve on the left and dips just below it on the right (a graze, not a large overshoot). 'R_k' centered inside the rectangle. 'x_{k-1}' and 'x_k' below the axis at the two edges, with short tick marks. Rotation arrow: a flattened ellipse ≈0.55 world units wide, ≈0.18 tall, centered on the y-axis at y ≈ 3.0, with an arrowhead on its right side indicating rotation into the screen.
PANEL (b) (axonometric, parallel projection so all circles render as congruent ellipses): y-axis vertical through the shell's center, arrowhead up, italic 'y' at top; x-axis running out to the right along the ground plane with arrowhead and italic 'x'. Shell centered on the y-axis: inner radius x_{k-1}, outer radius x_k, height f(x̄_k), bottom at y = 0. At default n = 6, k = 5 the ring reads thick-walled (inner radius ≈ 0.8 × outer) — reproduce that proportion rather than a razor-thin tube. The teal-tinted generating rectangle is the vertical slab of the shell nearest the viewer on the +x side, lying in the xy-plane. A short teal arc of y = f(x) passes over the shell's upper right. Italic 'S_k' just to the RIGHT of the shell at ≈0.6 of its height with a short leader line. Nested rings for the other strips and the ghost lathe of the full solid are HIDDEN by default (showAllShells = false).
TYPOGRAPHY: all math labels ('x', 'y', 'R_k', 'S_k', 'x_{k-1}', 'x_k') italic serif at ≈22px screen size; caption text ≈16px; panel letters '(a)'/'(b)' italic ≈18px. Labels must stay readable, never shrink below these sizes.
COLORS: curve and highlights teal #29B6BE; rectangle / generating-slab fill pale teal #B9DDD8 at ~60% opacity; shell body light gray #D0D0D0 at ~35% opacity with #6E6E6E silhouette ellipses; optional ghost solid #D0D0D0 at ~15%; axes and text near-black #1A1A1A; caption boxes white fill with #9A9A9A 1px border.
plan.notes: Use a THREE.OrthographicCamera for the whole scene so panel (b) renders with parallel ellipses like the textbook engraving; set a fixed isometric-ish pose (camera looking down the +x/+z diagonal, ~20° above horizon) and keep panel (a) strictly flat in a z = 0 plane facing the viewer — when 'View' is '(a) Rectangle' tween the camera to a dead-on front pose; when '(b) Shell' or 'Both', use the axonometric pose but keep panel (a)'s group billboarded to the camera so its linework never skews. Panel (a): Line/LineSegments for axes and curve plus ShapeGeometry for the shaded rectangle, all MeshBasicMaterial/LineBasicMaterial (unlit) so it reads as flat linework. Shell: two open-ended CylinderGeometry walls (thetaLength driven by sweepAngle) + two RingGeometry annuli (thetaLength matched) + two flat radial end-caps that appear whenever sweepAngle < 360; transparent, depthWrite:false, side DoubleSide, renderOrder sorted back-to-front. Draw dark silhouette ellipses with EllipseCurve→Line at the top and bottom of both walls for the outlined textbook look. factorHighlight: 'radius r' = thick teal arrow from the y-axis to x̄_k at mid-height; 'circumference 2πr' = teal band around the mid-surface that can unroll into a flat strip of width 2πr; 'height h' = vertical teal segment on the outer wall; 'thickness Δx' = highlighted band on the top annulus between the two radii. showAllShells uses one InstancedMesh of the ring geometry with per-instance scale; cap n at 24. All text via CSS2DRenderer HTML so italic math typesets crisply, stays screen-aligned during orbit, and honors the 22px/16px sizes. Orbit enabled only when panel (b) is visible.

authoredPrompt: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the shell method for computing volumes of solids of revolution about the y-axis. Panel (a): the 2D xy-plane showing a decreasing curve with a single rectangular strip Rk spanning from x_{k-1} to xk approximating the kth vertical strip of the region; a rotation arrow near the y-axis indicates revolution about that axis. Caption: Rectangle approximating the kth strip. Panel (b): a 3D view of the cylindrical shell Sk generated by revolving the rectangle about the y-axis, shown as a hollow cylindrical ring. Caption: Cylindrical shell generated by the rectangle. The figure introduces the shell method by showing how each thin vertical rectangle, when revolved, produces a cylindrical shell whose volume approximates the corresponding tubular portion of the solid.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for strip index k: select the kth rectangle in panel (a) and simultaneously highlight the corresponding cylindrical shell Sₖ in panel (b), displaying its radius, height, and volume
- Slider for number of strips n: increase n and watch the shells become thinner, with the total shell volume sum converging to the true solid volume
- Toggle shell formula factors: radius, height, circumference, and thickness highlight one at a time on the selected shell, showing where 2?r h ?x comes from.
authoredContext: As a rule, the tubes will have curved upper surfaces, so there will be no simple formulas for their volumes. However, if the strips are thin, then we can approximate each strip by a rectangle (Figure 5.3.4a). These rectangles, when revolved about the y-axis, will produce cylindrical shells whose volumes closely approximate the volumes of the tubes generated by the original strips (Figure 5.3.4b). We will show that by adding the volumes of the cylindrical shells we can obtain a Riemann sum that approximates the volume V, and by taking the limit of the Riemann sums we can obtain an integral for the exact volume V .
sourceQmd: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.3.4

demo_steps.title: The k th rectangle
demo_steps.narration: In the xy-plane the region under y = f(x) is cut into vertical strips. The k th strip is approximated by a rectangle R_k reaching from x_{k-1} to x_k, with the small rotation arrow reminding you the region will be spun about the y-axis.

demo_steps.title: Revolve it
demo_steps.narration: Revolving that rectangle about the y-axis sweeps out the cylindrical shell S_k: a tube with inner radius x_{k-1}, outer radius x_k, and the rectangle's height. Drag to see the hollow core.

demo_steps.title: Where 2πr h Δx comes from
demo_steps.narration: Highlight each factor in turn: the radius r to the axis, the circumference 2πr you would get by unrolling the wall, the height h of the rectangle, and the thickness Δx. Their product is the shell's volume.

demo_steps.title: Same thickness, different radius
demo_steps.narration: Slide k outward. The thickness never changes but the radius does, so the outer shells contribute far more volume than the inner ones — the x in 2πx f(x) is doing real work.

demo_steps.title: Many thin shells
demo_steps.narration: Increase n and the shells become thin nested tubes that fill the solid. The running sum of 2πx_k f(x_k)Δx closes in on the exact volume 2π∫₀⁴ x f(x) dx ≈ 90.48.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use f(x) = 3 − 0.15x² on 0 ≤ x ≤ 4 (f(0)=3, f(4)=0.6) — a concave-down decreasing curve matching the source. World units: x-axis drawn from −0.6 to 5.2, y-axis from −0.3 to 3.6; 1 world unit ≈ 1 axis unit, so the whole figure spans roughly 6 × 4 units. Δx = 4/n; strip k spans [x_{k-1}, x_k] = [(k−1)Δx, kΔx]; rectangle height h = f(x̄_k) at the midpoint; shell volume V_k = 2π x̄_k f(x̄_k) Δx; exact total 2π∫₀⁴ x(3−0.15x²)dx = 2π(14.4) ≈ 90.478. PANEL (a) LAYOUT (front-on, z = 0): y-axis vertical at x = 0 with arrowhead up and italic 'y' to its upper right; x-axis horizontal along y = 0 with arrowhead right and italic 'x' above it near the right end; the curve is drawn only over roughly 0.8 ≤ x ≤ 4.2 (it does not touch either axis); the rectangle sits on the x-axis with its top edge horizontal and slightly ABOVE the curve at its left edge and BELOW it at its right edge; label 'R_k' centered inside; 'x_{k-1}' and 'x_k' typeset below the axis at the two edges; the curved rotation arrow is a small horizontal ellipse (≈0.5 unit wide) around the y-axis at y ≈ 3.0 with an arrowhead on its right side pointing clockwise-forward. PANEL (b) LAYOUT: same axes, y-axis passing vertically through the center of the shell, x-axis passing horizontally through the shell's base; the shell is centered on the y-axis with inner radius x_{k-1}, outer radius x_k, height h, bottom at y = 0; italic 'S_k' sits just to the RIGHT of the shell at about 0.6h. In the source the ring looks thick (inner radius ≈ 0.55 × outer) because n is small — reproduce that at n = 6, k = 4. The teal-tinted generating rectangle is the vertical slab of the shell nearest the viewer-right, lying in the xy-plane at positive x. Draw a faint gray ghost of the full solid of revolution (radius 4, profile f) behind/around the shell so the shell reads as one layer of the solid. COLORS: curve and highlight teal #29B6BE; shell/rectangle fill pale teal #B9DDD8 at ~55% opacity; ghost solid and shell body light gray #D0D0D0 at ~35% opacity with #6E6E6E silhouette edges; axes and text near-black #1A1A1A; caption boxes white with #9A9A9A 1px border.
interactionPlan.notes: Build panel (a) with Line/LineLoop geometry in the z = 0 plane plus a ShapeGeometry for the shaded rectangle; keep it unlit (MeshBasicMaterial) so it reads as flat linework. Build the shell from two open-ended CylinderGeometry walls (outer radius x_k, inner radius x_{k-1}) plus two RingGeometry annuli for top and bottom, all with side: THREE.DoubleSide, transparent, depthWrite: false, and render-order sorted back-to-front to avoid transparency popping; add dark silhouette circles (EllipseCurve→Line) at top/bottom of each wall to reproduce the textbook's outlined look. Ghost solid = LatheGeometry from the profile f(x) sampled at 40 points, same translucent gray. Factor highlights: 'radius r' draws a thick teal segment from the y-axis to x̄_k at mid-height with an arrow; 'circumference 2πr' animates a teal torus/ring band around the shell's mid-surface, optionally unrolling into a flat strip of width 2πr; 'height h' draws a vertical teal segment on the outer wall; 'thickness Δx' highlights the top annulus band between the two radii. Labels (y, x, R_k, S_k, x_k, x_{k-1}, captions, (a)/(b)) as CSS2DRenderer HTML so italic math typesets crisply and stays screen-aligned during orbit. Orbit should be enabled only when the shell panel is visible; lock the camera to the front-on pose in panel (a) and tween between poses when the toggle changes. Cap rendered strips at n = 24 and reuse a single instanced shell geometry when drawing all shells for performance.

discrepancies: The source is a side-by-side two-panel figure (a)+(b); the generated default view shows only panel (a) with panel (b) hidden behind a toggle, so at first glance the defining cylindrical-shell image of the source is absent (a 'Both' default would match the source composition).

Panel (a) content is rendered small and offset toward the left of the canvas, leaving a large empty region; labels (R_k, x_{k-1}, x_k, caption box) end up noticeably smaller and less prominent than in the source, where R_k and the caption are large and legible.

The teal curve in (a) drops more steeply and extends well past x_k to near the x-axis, whereas the source curve is a gentle shallow arc that ends just beyond the rectangle; the rectangle also sits farther right relative to the curve than in the source.
Panel (b) uses a perspective camera whereas the source (b) is drawn with a flat, near-orthographic axonometric look (parallel silhouette ellipses, no convergence).

The source (b) shows a clearly hollow outer ghost solid with one prominent inner ring pair; the generated (b) adds n extra nested strip rings at every partition point, which is extra annotation not in the original.

demo_steps.title: The two panels side by side
demo_steps.narration: On the left, the region under y = f(x) is cut into vertical strips and the k th strip is approximated by the rectangle R_k. On the right, that same rectangle spun about the y-axis has become the cylindrical shell S_k.

demo_steps.title: The k th rectangle
demo_steps.narration: Look at panel (a) alone: R_k runs from x_{k-1} to x_k and its top edge just grazes the curve. The small rotation arrow at the top of the y-axis reminds you the region will be spun about that axis.

demo_steps.title: Revolve it
demo_steps.narration: Drag the revolution angle from 0° to 360°. The rectangle sweeps a fan, then closes into a tube with inner radius x_{k-1}, outer radius x_k and height f(x̄_k). Orbit to see the hollow core.

demo_steps.title: Where 2πr·h·Δx comes from
demo_steps.narration: Highlight each factor in turn. Unrolling the wall gives a flat slab of width 2πr, height h and thickness Δx — so the shell's volume is the product of those three.

demo_steps.title: Same thickness, different radius
demo_steps.narration: Slide k inward and outward. The thickness Δx never changes but the radius does, so outer shells contribute far more volume than inner ones — the factor x in 2πx f(x) is doing real work.

demo_steps.title: Nesting the shells
demo_steps.narration: Turn on all n shells and raise n. The nested tubes fill the solid and ΣV_k = Σ2πx̄_k f(x̄_k)Δx closes in on the exact volume 2π∫₀^{3.2} x f(x) dx ≈ 67.0.

plan.geometry_notes:
FUNCTION: f(x) = 2.8 − 0.14x² on 0 ≤ x ≤ 3.2 (f(0)=2.8, f(3.2)=1.37) — a GENTLE, nearly flat concave-down arc, NOT a steep decay. Δx = 3.2/n; strip k spans [(k−1)Δx, kΔx]; midpoint x̄_k; rectangle height h = f(x̄_k); V_k = 2π x̄_k f(x̄_k) Δx; exact total 2π∫₀^{3.2} x(2.8−0.14x²)dx = 2π(10.666) ≈ 67.02.
FRAME LAYOUT (default 'Both'): panel (a) occupies the LEFT half, panel (b) the RIGHT half, their baselines aligned; each caption box sits centered under its own drawing with the italic '(a)' / '(b)' beneath. The pair should fill ~0.74 of the frame height — zoom in so text is prominent.
PANEL (a) (flat, front-on, z = 0): y-axis vertical at x = 0 spanning y = −0.3…3.4 with arrowhead up and italic 'y' at its upper right; x-axis horizontal along y = 0 spanning x = −0.5…4.0 with arrowhead right and italic 'x' just above its right end. THE CURVE IS DRAWN ONLY FROM x ≈ 0.45 TO x ≈ x_k + 0.55 (default ≈ 3.2) — it starts in mid-air near the y-axis and stops shortly after the rectangle's right edge; it never reaches the x-axis. Rectangle R_k sits on the x-axis, left edge at x_{k-1}, right edge at x_k, top edge horizontal at height f(x̄_k) so it pokes slightly above the curve on the left and dips just below it on the right (a graze, not a large overshoot). 'R_k' centered inside the rectangle. 'x_{k-1}' and 'x_k' below the axis at the two edges, with short tick marks. Rotation arrow: a flattened ellipse ≈0.55 world units wide, ≈0.18 tall, centered on the y-axis at y ≈ 3.0, with an arrowhead on its right side indicating rotation into the screen.
PANEL (b) (axonometric, parallel projection so all circles render as congruent ellipses): y-axis vertical through the shell's center, arrowhead up, italic 'y' at top; x-axis running out to the right along the ground plane with arrowhead and italic 'x'. Shell centered on the y-axis: inner radius x_{k-1}, outer radius x_k, height f(x̄_k), bottom at y = 0. At default n = 6, k = 5 the ring reads thick-walled (inner radius ≈ 0.8 × outer) — reproduce that proportion rather than a razor-thin tube. The teal-tinted generating rectangle is the vertical slab of the shell nearest the viewer on the +x side, lying in the xy-plane. A short teal arc of y = f(x) passes over the shell's upper right. Italic 'S_k' just to the RIGHT of the shell at ≈0.6 of its height with a short leader line. Nested rings for the other strips and the ghost lathe of the full solid are HIDDEN by default (showAllShells = false).
TYPOGRAPHY: all math labels ('x', 'y', 'R_k', 'S_k', 'x_{k-1}', 'x_k') italic serif at ≈22px screen size; caption text ≈16px; panel letters '(a)'/'(b)' italic ≈18px. Labels must stay readable, never shrink below these sizes.
COLORS: curve and highlights teal #29B6BE; rectangle / generating-slab fill pale teal #B9DDD8 at ~60% opacity; shell body light gray #D0D0D0 at ~35% opacity with #6E6E6E silhouette ellipses; optional ghost solid #D0D0D0 at ~15%; axes and text near-black #1A1A1A; caption boxes white fill with #9A9A9A 1px border.
plan.notes: Use a THREE.OrthographicCamera for the whole scene so panel (b) renders with parallel ellipses like the textbook engraving; set a fixed isometric-ish pose (camera looking down the +x/+z diagonal, ~20° above horizon) and keep panel (a) strictly flat in a z = 0 plane facing the viewer — when 'View' is '(a) Rectangle' tween the camera to a dead-on front pose; when '(b) Shell' or 'Both', use the axonometric pose but keep panel (a)'s group billboarded to the camera so its linework never skews. Panel (a): Line/LineSegments for axes and curve plus ShapeGeometry for the shaded rectangle, all MeshBasicMaterial/LineBasicMaterial (unlit) so it reads as flat linework. Shell: two open-ended CylinderGeometry walls (thetaLength driven by sweepAngle) + two RingGeometry annuli (thetaLength matched) + two flat radial end-caps that appear whenever sweepAngle < 360; transparent, depthWrite:false, side DoubleSide, renderOrder sorted back-to-front. Draw dark silhouette ellipses with EllipseCurve→Line at the top and bottom of both walls for the outlined textbook look. factorHighlight: 'radius r' = thick teal arrow from the y-axis to x̄_k at mid-height; 'circumference 2πr' = teal band around the mid-surface that can unroll into a flat strip of width 2πr; 'height h' = vertical teal segment on the outer wall; 'thickness Δx' = highlighted band on the top annulus between the two radii. showAllShells uses one InstancedMesh of the ring geometry with per-instance scale; cap n at 24. All text via CSS2DRenderer HTML so italic math typesets crisply, stays screen-aligned during orbit, and honors the 22px/16px sizes. Orbit enabled only when panel (b) is visible.
